subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex app-server TCP and Unix WebSocket handshakes share an unconditional 30-second cutoff and listener-dependent error forwarding?
rationale: The mechanism is dependency-supported and well proven for stalled peers, but the deadline and event semantics alter existing transport behavior in ways that CI cannot establish as compatible for every supported deployment.

options.title: Accept the shared deadline
options.body: Land the patch after confirming that 30 seconds safely covers supported TCP, proxy, and Unix upgrade conditions.

options.title: Separate transport deadlines
options.body: Use distinct or owner-supplied deadlines if experimental remote TCP and supported local Unix connections have different latency envelopes.

options.title: Narrow the event change
options.body: Add the handshake deadline while preserving prior error forwarding if listener-dependent suppression is not an intended transport contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the shared deadline
recommendation.body: Land the patch after confirming that 30 seconds safely covers supported TCP, proxy, and Unix upgrade conditions.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-level ownership makes this the best available routing candidate for the compatibility decision, though feature-history attribution is incomplete.
